A.title: Does merging DeepSeekR1, QwQ, and SkyT1 into FuseO1 improve date calculation accuracy over DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B?
A.body:
A 2025 Reddit post shared a Fusion model called FuseO1-DeepSeekR1-QwQ-SkyT1-32B-Preview, which merges DeepSeekR1, QwQ, and SkyT1 32B models. The user tested this merged model against DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B using ollama with a 32k context and Q8_0 KV Cache.

The key question is whether combining these models actually yields better accuracy on tasks like date calculations, or if the merge introduces tradeoffs that might impact specific capabilities. Since the test environment details are limited, it’s unclear how generalizable the results are.

Has anyone else compared merged models like this to their base components for date or time-related reasoning? What practical differences have you observed in accuracy or consistency?

B.title: Insights and Questions on Merged LLM Performance from a 2025 User Report
B.body: A user shared a comparison between a merged LLM, FuseO1-DeepSeekR1-QwQ-SkyT1-32B-Preview, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B on r/LocalLLaMA. The merged model reportedly excelled at a file-packing problem and correctly computed a date difference of 19,121 days, while the other model gave a wrong result. Additionally, the merged model solved a river crossing riddle with a single crossing, but DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B got stuck in an infinite loop. The test environment used ollama with IQ4_XS quantization and a 32k context window with Q8_0 KV Cache. Since the source is a single user’s report from early 2025, it raises questions about how merging models affects reasoning and stability. Does merging generally improve logical consistency, or might it introduce unexpected behaviors? What are the best practices to evaluate such merges beyond anecdotal tests? Sharing experiences or benchmarks on merged models could help clarify their practical benefits and limitations.
